# World templates use the existing authored-base initialization boundary

Date: 2026-09-13. Status: accepted for this isolated implementation.

The approved demonstrations previously lived in separate profiles. Restoring
their portable backups into one profile would replace its complete data domain.
Instead publish immutable formal source closures as shipped authored starters.
The existing world factory creates one new native world per operation and the
existing managed-source initializer builds and checks it normally.

No new SQLite ownership, IPC privilege, arbitrary import path, native RPC, model
tool, or general archive importer is introduced. Publication is an operator build
step. The runtime trusts only shipped hash-pinned template metadata and files.
The renderer selects IDs and receives bounded previews. Development and release
use the same materializer and runtime distribution manifest.

Reusing source means preserving world-local component identity within its new
world scope. Global rewriting of arbitrary script identifiers would not be a safe
copy operation. Initial state must be captured from exact source defaults, rather
than copied from the publisher's played save. Existing native initialization and
source transactions retain authority over durable world data and readiness.

Large demonstrations exceed one source request. Serialize source installation
into retryable batches; retain existing native request/project limits. Reopening
an interrupted initialization reads the durable source index and installs only
missing files, then uses the ordinary check and first-load path.
